description: Golden routing grid for the continental water pass (rivers and lakes, Task 2). A 4 x 5 GridGraph, row 0 north, at 1,000 m spacing; column 0 is ocean at -10 m. Cells are [row, col]. receiver is null for ocean. q holds discharge per case; null for ocean. Each case gives the evaporation capacity per basin node and the lake it makes (Task 3); the Python reference (Task 11) reads the same file.

A.description: unit runoff on every land node, no evaporation

B.description: unit runoff; each basin node evaporates up to 2 m3/s. Open: the basin's 8 m3/s of capacity is below its 12 m3/s inflow, so it spills 4 m3/s over the rim (1, 1). Inside the basin, discharge re-accumulates along the routing receivers into the exit.

C.description: unit runoff; each basin node evaporates up to 5 m3/s. Terminal: the 1 m group holds 5 m3/s, the 2 m group 15 more, so 12 m3/s stands 7/15 of the way from 2 m to the 3 m spill: level 2 + 7/15 m. The lake's nodes are sinks and keep their own water; nothing reaches the rim.
